page: Amazon Web Services c7a.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz, configured with 1 physical core, 1 virtual CPU, and 1 thread per core. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 4 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 2.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or a GPU, and it has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 25%. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench is weak, falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block bandwidth in the bottom 10% and large block read bandwidth in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels. For lightweight AI tasks, the instance achieves average text generation speeds of 107.26 tokens per second on a small 135M LLM, though prompt processing is weak at 287.57 tokens per second.

The c7a.medium offers a cost-effective entry point to dedicated AMD EPYC Gen7 hardware, avoiding the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances. The primary tradeoff is the strict resource constraint of a single vCPU and 2.0 GB of RAM, which limits its utility for parallel processing, software compilation, and database operations, all of which scored in the bottom 10% in Passmark testing. This server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, simple text processing, or small-scale development and testing tasks that require dedicated CPU execution without high memory or network throughput.
